transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, doctor, I'm here because... well, honestly, it’s just a massive headache and I don't even know where to start, but I guess I came because of my husband’s sister. She has been... well, she’s been working this family business from the inside, just digging her claws in. It’s been going on for a while now, and I see exactly what she’s doing. She wants to get control of the money, every last dime of it, and she’s trying to push me completely out of any decisions. 

I mean, I used to be in the loop, you know? My husband and I used to talk about things. But now, she’s always whispering with him, always moving paperwork around or closing laptops when I walk into the room. And the thing is, everyone else—my husband, his folks—they all just try to smooth it over. They pat my hand and say, "Oh, she’s just trying to help out," or "You’re making a mountain out of a molehill, let it go." 

But I’m not blind, and I'm not stupid. I know what I’ve been seeing. I've been watching her operate for more than a year now, day in and day out, and you can't tell me I'm making it up when the proof is right there in how she looks at me and how the bank statements suddenly don't come to the house anymore. I just... I can't take the sneaking around anymore, and it drives me crazy that no one will listen to me about what she's really up to.
Do you think your husband's sister is plotting against you specifically?

Oh, absolutely. It is one hundred percent directed right at me. It’s not just some accident or her being bossy. Like I was trying to say before, I came in here today specifically because my husband’s sister has been working this family business—which, by the way, was doing just fine before she started sticking her nose into every little thing—just so she can get total control of the money. And the whole point of her doing that is to push *me* out of the decisions. Me. Not her brother, not his parents. Just me. 

It’s like she’s had this... this plan, you know? And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—and believe me, my husband’s parents are the absolute worst about this, they are always making excuses for her, saying, "Oh, she’s just good with numbers," or "She’s family, she means well." But they don't see the little smirks. They don't see how she physically steps between me and my husband when we're talking about the accounts. I know what I’ve been seeing. I really do. I’ve been watching this happen for more than a year now, over a whole year of this slow, deliberate squeezing me out of my own life. 

Just the other day... well, maybe it was a couple weeks ago, time just blurs together when you're this stressed out... but she made this little comment about how "some people" just don't have the head for the financials. She meant me. I know she did. I might not have finished high school, but I’ve managed a household and kept our bills paid for decades, so I know exactly how money works! But she uses all these big words and shuffles her little folders around just to make me look foolish in front of him, so she can have it all to herself. So yes, doctor, it is very much a plot against me, and I just... I can't be the only one who sees it!
Do you think there's any possibility that you might be misinterpreting your husband's sister's actions?

Misinterpreting? No. No, doctor, I really don't think I am. I know people want to think that, because it's easier, isn't it? It's easier to just say, 'Oh, she's just confused' or 'She doesn't understand how the accounts work.' But I have eyes in my head. 

Like I was trying to explain earlier, the whole reason I came in here today is because my husband’s sister has been working this family business from the inside for one specific reason—so she can get total control of the money and push me completely out of all the decisions. And I'm home all day, right? I manage our household, I don't go off to an office, so I'm the one who used to get the mail, I see the calls coming in, I notice the little changes in how things are run. I've had the time to really watch her operate. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—my husband, his parents, all of them just patting my arm and acting like I'm just getting worked up over nothing—I know what I’ve been seeing. 

I really do. I’ve been watching this happen for more than a year now. A whole year of her intercepting the bank statements, changing the passwords on the online accounts, and talking down to me like I'm some sort of child just because I didn't get my diploma. You don't need to have finished twelfth grade to know when you're being robbed blind in your own life! I mean, if it was just one time, or just one weird comment, maybe I'd say, okay, maybe I misread that. Maybe I'm just tired. But every single day? For over twelve months? The way she looks at me when she hands my husband a stack of papers to sign and literally turns her shoulder so I can't read the fine print? That's not me misinterpreting things, doctor. That's a deliberate strategy. She knows exactly what she's doing, and it just exhausts me that I have to fight so hard just to prove what's happening right in front of everyone's faces.
Do you think there's anything that could happen that would make you change your mind about your husband's sister plotting against you?

Change my mind? Well... I mean, honestly, doctor? No. I don't see how anything could just magically erase what's been happening right in front of me. It's not like a switch you can just flip off, you know? It’s... it’s my everyday life. I suppose if she suddenly packed her bags, handed over all the account keys, and moved to Timbuktu, maybe then I’d say, 'Okay, she's finally stopped.' But even then, the damage is already done, isn't it? 

Because, like I keep trying to explain—and I know I sound like a broken record, but it’s the whole reason I came in here to see you—my husband’s sister has been working this family business just so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. That is a fact. That hasn't changed. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over... you know, making me a cup of tea, telling me to go relax, acting like I just don't understand the 'complexities' of the business because I didn't finish high school... I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now! 

You can't unsee over twelve months of someone systematically trying to erase you. I mean, just think about it from my perspective. If someone came into your house, rearranged your life, hid your mail, and then smiled sweetly at your spouse while doing it... you wouldn't just change your mind because someone patted your hand and told you it was all fine, would you? You’d trust your own two eyes. And my eyes work perfectly fine, thank you very much. I just wish someone, anyone, would actually look at the paperwork with me instead of just acting like I'm the one who's being unreasonable, because if you saw the way she organizes those files, you'd see exactly what I mean...
Do you think your husband's sister would be plotting against you if you weren't involved in the family business?

If I wasn't involved? Well... I'm not really sure what you mean by that, doctor, or how to even answer that. Because I'm his wife. I mean, I don't know if she'd still be plotting if there wasn't a business at all, or if I wasn't in the picture... I really couldn't tell you. Maybe she'd find some other way to try and ruin my life, or maybe she'd just ignore me completely, I don't know. I can't read her mind about things that aren't happening. 

But the thing is, I *am* involved, because it's my husband, and it's our money. I might not be the one down there doing the actual labor, and like I said, I'm home managing the house, but the money that comes out of that business is what pays our mortgage. It's what pays for the groceries, the electric bill, everything. I've managed all of that for years. So when she starts messing with the accounts and trying to push me out of the decisions, she's messing with my actual livelihood. 

Would she do it if the business wasn't there? I just... I don't have an answer for that. It's a big 'what if' and I don't really have the energy to guess about what-ifs right now. What I do know is what's actually happening right now in reality. And in reality, like I came in here to tell you, she has been working this family business from the inside just to get total control of the money and push me out. That's what is happening. And honestly, it doesn't even matter if she would or wouldn't do it in some imaginary world where the business doesn't exist, because we live in this world. And in this world, I've been watching her for over a year, day in and day out, intercepting things, whispering to my husband, trying to make me look like I don't know how to balance a checkbook just because I didn't graduate. So I can't really sit here and guess about what she might do in some other situation, because I'm too busy trying to survive what she's doing to me right now. I just need someone to see what she's actually doing instead of asking me what she might do if things were different.
Do you think your husband's sister would stop plotting against you if you and your husband were to divorce?

Divorce? Oh, well... I mean, I suppose that would certainly get her what she wants, wouldn't it? If I were gone, completely out of the picture, she wouldn't have to worry about me catching on to her little scheme. But... divorce? That's... that's my marriage, doctor. We've built a life together, a home. I've taken care of him and that house for years, and the thought of just walking away and letting her win... it just makes my blood boil. 

But to answer your question, yes, I suppose she'd probably stop plotting against me specifically if we divorced, because she'd have already succeeded. She'd have him all to herself, and the business, and the accounts. But see, that's exactly why I'm fighting this. That's why I'm here. Because like I've been saying this whole time—and I know I keep repeating myself, but it's just so crucial that someone understands—my husband's sister has been working this family business from the inside for the sole purpose of getting control of the money and pushing me completely out of the decisions. 

And no matter how much my husband or his parents try to smooth it over, telling me I'm just stressed or that I don't understand the finances because I didn't finish high school... I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. Over twelve months of this! I've seen the way she maneuvers, the way she hides the mail, the way she smiles that tight little smile when she gets him to sign something without me looking. I'm not going to just divorce my husband and hand her the keys to my life. I've been watching her operate for over a year, and I know exactly what she's doing, even if everyone else wants to pretend I'm just making a fuss over nothing. I just need someone to actually look at the evidence with me, instead of asking me if I'm going to leave my own marriage just to make her stop!
Can you think of any reason why your husband's sister would want to help with the family business that doesn't involve plotting against you?

Any other reason? Well... I mean, if you listen to my in-laws, they’ve got a whole list of reasons ready to go, don't they? They’ll tell you she’s just 'so good with numbers' or that she’s just being a supportive little sister because the business has been getting busier and my husband is just so overwhelmed. Even he tells me, 'Honey, she’s just trying to take some stress off my plate, you don't need to worry about it.' And sure, maybe on the surface, to somebody who just walked in off the street, it looks like this nice, sweet, picture-perfect family pitching in to help each other out. 

But you see, doctor, you can't just look at the surface. You have to look at what's actually happening underneath all those sweet smiles and 'let me help you with that's. Because... and I know I keep coming back to this, I know I'm probably talking your ear off about it, but it is literally the entire reason I came in to see you today... my husband’s sister has been working this family business for one specific reason, and that is so she can get control of the money and push me completely out of the decisions. That's the long and short of it. 

And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—and believe me, they try all the time, patting my shoulder, telling me I’m just overthinking things, treating me like I'm some sort of simpleton who can't grasp basic math just because I dropped out in the eleventh grade—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now! You don't just watch someone for over twelve months, day after day, inching their way into the bank accounts, moving funds around, and intercepting the mail, and think, 'Oh, she's just being so helpful.' It's not helpful when she's deliberately cutting the wife out of the picture. I mean, think about it rationally. If she really just wanted to help the family, why wouldn't she sit down with both of us? Why wouldn't she show me the books, too? Instead, it's all hush-hush, closed doors, whispering in the hallway... so no, I can't think of a single innocent reason, because there isn't one. She knows exactly what she's doing.
Is there anything your husband's sister could do or say that would make you think she is not plotting against you?

Do or say? Well... honestly, doctor, what could she possibly say at this point? 'Oh, I'm sorry, I didn't mean to hide the bank statements'? 'Oops, I accidentally left you off the email with the accountant'? Words are just air. She could sit right in that chair next to me and swear on a stack of Bibles that she’s just trying to be a helpful little sister, but I wouldn't believe a single syllable of it. Because people can say whatever they want, can't they? They can smile right to your face, offer to pour you a cup of coffee, all while they're sliding the rug right out from under your feet. 

And as for doing something... I mean, what, is she going to completely quit the business? Pack her bags and move to another state? Even if she did step away today and hand over the books, I'd just be waiting for the other shoe to drop. I'd be looking over my shoulder wondering what her next angle is, or what she secretly set up before she left. Because... and I know I sound like a broken record, I really do, but I have to keep saying it so you understand—I came in here today because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of the decisions. That is the absolute reality of my life right now. 

And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—my husband making excuses for her, his parents telling me I'm just being sensitive, everybody treating me like I'm just some paranoid housewife who can't grasp what's going on because I didn't get my diploma—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. You can't just erase over twelve months of sneaking around, the whispering in the kitchen when they think I'm out of earshot, the way she physically blocks me from seeing the ledger... you can't erase all of that with a simple 'I'm sorry' or by suddenly acting nice. She's already shown me exactly who she is and what she's after. She's shown her hand. So no, doctor, there isn't some magic word she could say or some little gesture she could do that would just wipe my memory clean and make me trust her. I've seen too much. I've been living it every single day, and I'm not going to just turn off my brain and pretend it isn't happening.
Is there anything that could happen that would make you doubt your husband's sister is plotting against you?

Doubt? Make me doubt it? Well... I mean, think about what you're asking me, doctor. You're asking if there's some kind of magical event, some... some sign from above or some sudden change of heart that would make me think I've just been imagining things this whole time. But how can I doubt my own two eyes? How can I doubt the reality of my everyday life? 

It’s not like I just woke up one Tuesday morning and decided to be suspicious for no good reason. This has been a slow, agonizing process. I've spent days, weeks, just sitting at my kitchen table after my husband leaves for work, going over the bits of paper I manage to find, thinking about the phone calls she suddenly ends the second I walk into the room. You don't just doubt something that is constantly staring you in the face. 

Look, I know I keep hammering this exact same point home, and you're probably writing down in your notes that I just won't let it go, but I have to make you see the reality of my situation. I came here to see you because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. That is the absolute truth of it. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—bringing me coffee, telling me I should just relax and let them handle the hard math because I didn't finish high school, treating me like I'm just a fragile little bird—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

Over a year! You don't just watch someone methodically take over your livelihood for over twelve months and then suddenly wake up one day and say, 'Gee, maybe I'm wrong.' If I start doubting what I know for a fact is happening, if I let them convince me that I'm just confused and she's actually some kind of saint, then she wins. The trap snaps shut. She gets the money, she gets the business, and I get pushed out into the cold with nothing to show for all my years of marriage. So no, I won't doubt it. I can't doubt it, because the evidence is right there, every single day, whether anybody else wants to admit it or not.
Have you ever caught your husband's sister doing something that you considered to be part of her plot against you, and if so, what was it?

Caught her? Oh, absolutely. More times than I can count, honestly. Just... well, just take last Tuesday as a perfect example. Or maybe it was Wednesday? No, it was Tuesday, because the garbage trucks were coming down the street and they always make that awful racket. Anyway, I was coming down the stairs, and I had my soft slippers on so I didn't make a sound. I wasn't trying to sneak up on her, I was just walking around in my own house, you know? And I look into the front hallway, and there she is, standing by the console table where we keep the mail. 

Now, she was sifting through the stack—which she has no business doing in the first place—and I watched her, clear as day, pull out a thick envelope. It had the bank's logo right there in the corner window. It was the quarterly statements. And instead of leaving it for my husband or, heaven forbid, handing it to me, she folds it in half and shoves it right into the bottom of her big leather purse. 

When I cleared my throat, I swear she nearly jumped out of her skin. She whipped around, plastered on this fake, sugary smile, and said, 'Oh! Good morning! I was just checking to see if the new supplier catalog arrived.' And when I asked her flat out what she had just put in her bag, she didn't even blink. She looked me dead in the eye and said, 'Just some old receipts I need to take home and file.' Receipts! In a sealed envelope from the bank? I might not have a high school diploma, doctor, but I am not stupid. I know what a bank statement looks like.

And it just... it brings me right back to what I’ve been telling you this whole time. I know I keep saying the exact same thing, and I'm sure you're tired of hearing it, but it’s because it’s the absolute truth. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. That is exactly what she is doing. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—like my husband coming home later that night and telling me she probably was just organizing receipts and that I'm making a mountain out of a molehill—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

You don't just accidentally hide a bank statement in your purse. And that's not even the only time! There was another incident, maybe three weeks ago, when I walked into the home office and she was on the computer. The second the door creaked, she slammed the laptop shut so hard I thought she was going to crack the screen. She said she was just 'updating the antivirus,' but her face was completely red and she couldn't look me in the eye. So yes, I catch her doing things all the time, but she always has some slick, ready-made excuse waiting on the tip of her tongue, and everybody else just eats it right up.
Do you think your husband is aware of his sister's plot against you?

Aware? That’s... well, doctor, that is the million-dollar question, isn't it? I ask myself that every single night when I'm lying in bed staring at the ceiling listening to him snore. I honestly don't know. I really don't. 

Because on the one hand, how could he not see it? He's a smart man, we've been married a long time, and he's right there in the house with us. He sees her hovering over the ledger, he sees the way she talks down to me. But on the other hand... is he actually aware of what she's really doing? I just don't know if he's playing dumb because it's easier than confronting his own flesh and blood, or if he's genuinely just that blind to it all. 

You see, his family has always had this... this dynamic. His sister has always been the golden child, the one who understands business and margins and all those fancy corporate words. And he's always just let her take the reins whenever she wants. So when I try to sit him down—like just last Sunday, we were having pot roast, just the two of us for once because she was out doing who knows what, and I tried to lay it all out for him. I said, 'Look at what she's doing with the accounts.' And he just sighed, rubbed his temples, and told me I was overthinking things again. He always says that. 'You're overthinking, honey.' Or 'She's just trying to take some stress off our plates.' 

And it just frustrates me to tears, it really does. Because I know I keep bringing it back to this, and I know I sound like a broken record, but I have to make it clear why I'm even sitting in this chair talking to you today. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. That is the absolute reality of what is happening under our roof. 

And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—especially my own husband, patting my hand and telling me to just let her handle the complicated math because I didn't finish high school and shouldn't worry my pretty little head about it—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. So, is he aware? Sometimes I think he has to be, because nobody is that oblivious. But then I think... maybe she's just got him so wrapped around her little finger that he can't see the forest for the trees. He just doesn't want to see it. Because if he actually admitted what she was doing, he'd have to stand up to her, and he hates conflict. He always has. Whenever there's a problem, he just buries his head in the sand and hopes it blows over... so I just... I don't know what he really knows anymore.
Do you think your husband is in on his sister's plot against you?

In on it? Like, actively helping her plan it all out? No... no, I don't think so. I really don't. I mean, I've thought about it, of course I have, because when you're in my shoes you end up questioning absolutely everything. You sit there in the evening, watching television, and you look over at him asleep in his recliner and you just wonder, 'Are you part of this? Are you laughing at me behind my back?' But... no. He just isn't built that way. 

He doesn't have a malicious bone in his body, bless his heart. He's just... well, he's a path of least resistance kind of man. Always has been. Like last year when the gutters were leaking right over the front porch, and instead of calling the roofer who messed it up to demand they come back and fix it, he just put a plastic bucket down for three whole weeks because he didn't want to make a fuss. That's exactly who he is. So the idea of him actually sitting down with his sister and scheming? Whispering in the corner about how to hide the accounts and push me out of the picture? No. He wouldn't have the stomach for it. 

Plus, he's a terrible liar. Whenever he tries to keep a secret, even something small like what he got me for my birthday, he gets this little twitch over his left eye and he completely avoids making eye contact with me. I haven't seen any of that. What I see is just a man who is tired from working all day and wants to come home, eat his dinner in peace, and not deal with any drama whatsoever. He lets her run roughshod over the business because it's just easier for him than telling her 'no' and dealing with one of her tantrums. 

So no, I don't have any reason to believe he's actually plotting with her. It's all her doing. She's the one pulling the strings, and he's just... he's just a pawn, really. He's not the one driving the getaway car, so to speak. He just completely refuses to open his eyes and see that she's stealing the car in the first place! If I truly thought he was in on it, I don't think I could stay in that house another minute, but I really, truly believe it's just her.
Do you think your husband knows that you believe his sister is plotting against you?

Oh, he knows. He absolutely knows. I mean... I don't just sit in silence and let it eat at me, doctor. I've told him straight to his face, more times than I can count. 

Just... well, just yesterday morning, for instance. He was looking for his good silver watch, the one his dad gave him before he passed, and we were rummaging through the bedroom dresser trying to find it. And out of nowhere, I just had to stop, and I looked right at him and said, 'You know what she's doing, don't you?' And he did that heavy sigh. You know the one? That deep, tired sigh husbands do when they want you to just drop a subject and move on. He told me I was getting myself all worked up over nothing again. 

But I tell him exactly what I tell you. I don't sugarcoat it. I tell him straight out that I came to see a doctor because his sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. I know I've told you that same exact thing already, and I know I probably sound like a broken record by now, but I have to keep saying it because it is exactly what is happening. And I tell him, no matter how folks try to smooth it over—no matter how many times he pats my arm and tells me I'm just stressed or that I don't understand the paperwork because I didn't finish high school—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. 

So yes, he is fully aware of what I believe. He just chooses to treat me like I'm some sort of... of hysterical woman who watches too many soap operas. He’ll say things like, 'Now, honey, you know how her personality is, she just likes to be in charge of the details.' But liking details and actively plotting to ruin my standing in my own family are two very different things! It’s like talking to a brick wall sometimes. I lay out all the evidence for him, like the bank statements in the purse and the way she slams her computer shut, and he just... he just refuses to engage with it. He knows exactly what I think about her, but I think it’s just easier for him to pretend I'm the one with the problem than to admit his sister is a snake in the grass.
Is there anything that could make you completely change your mind about your husband's sister plotting against you?

Change my mind? Oh... well, doctor, I just... I don't even know how to answer that, because it would take an absolute miracle. Or an act of Congress, maybe. I mean, what would it even look like for me to change my mind at this point? She would have to march right into my living room, sit down on my floral sofa, look me dead in the eye, and confess to every single thing she's done. She'd have to hand over every single ledger, every bank statement, and give up all the passwords she's changed. And honestly? Even if she did all of that, I'd probably still think she was just trying to pull a fast one on me, maybe to make herself look like the bigger person in front of my husband. 

Because you have to understand, I haven't just imagined this out of thin air. I don't just sit around making up stories to cause trouble. I've spent days, weeks, just agonizing over every little detail. Like last month, when she 'accidentally' left the new supplier contracts in the trunk of her car when we were supposed to go over them together. Or how she suddenly decided the business needed a new accountant, someone she went to college with, without even asking me what I thought. It's always something with her. Always some little maneuver. 

So, no. I really don't think anything could change my mind. I know I keep bringing it back to this, and I know I've said it to you a hundred times already today, but I have to make sure you're really hearing me, because it's the entire reason I'm sitting in this room. I came because my husband’s sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions. That is just the plain and simple truth of it. 

And no matter how folks try to smooth it over—no matter how many times my husband tells me to calm down, or people treat me like I'm just some uneducated housewife who doesn't understand big important business things—I know what I’ve been seeing for more than a year now. You can't just erase fourteen months of watching someone slowly steal your life and your security out from under you just because they smile at you and bring over a casserole on a Sunday. You just can't unsee it once you've opened your eyes. So no, doctor, nothing is going to change my mind. I know exactly what she is.
Do you think your belief about your husband's sister plotting against you could be wrong?

Wrong? Me, wrong about this? Doctor, I just... I don't even know how you can ask me that after everything I've just laid out for you. I know sometimes people get things mixed up, sure. I know I didn't finish high school, and maybe I don't use all the right corporate vocabulary when I'm explaining things, but I am not stupid. And I am certainly not wrong. 

If I were wrong, I would be the happiest woman in the county. I really would. I would throw a parade, I would bake her a three-tier chocolate cake myself and hand-deliver it to her front porch! Because it would mean my life isn't falling apart. But you see, I can't be wrong, because I live with this day in and day out. I see the way she hovers over the ledgers, the way she talks over me at family dinners the second the shop gets brought up. 

I know I keep coming back to this same exact point, and I know I've repeated it to you three or four times already today, but I really need you to understand my purpose for being here. I came because my husband's sister has been working this family business so she can get control of the money and push me out of decisions entirely. That is the reality of the situation. And no matter how folks try to smooth it over... you know, patting my hand, telling me I'm just overthinking it, treating me like I'm just a bored housewife who doesn't get how things operate... I know what I've been seeing for more than a year now. 

It is exactly like... well, imagine you are standing in your own kitchen watching a pot boil over on the stove, water spilling everywhere, making a huge mess, and everyone else in the room is just standing there telling you the water isn't even hot. That is what my life has been like for the past fourteen months. You don't just imagine someone slowly boxing you out of your own livelihood and stealing your peace of mind. You feel it happening, step by step. So, no, doctor. I don't think I'm wrong. Not for a single second. I know what I know.
Do you think your feelings about your husband's sister could be affected by your own stress or anxiety?

Stress? Anxiety? Well... I mean, of course I’m stressed, doctor! Anyone would be stressed if they were walking in my shoes right now. But my stress isn't making me imagine things, if that's what you're getting at. It's the other way around. The stress is coming directly from what she is doing to me. 

My husband tries to pull that exact same card, you know. He’ll come into the kitchen while I’m pacing, and he'll say, 'Honey, your nerves are just shot, you're just feeling anxious because the shop is getting busier.'
